Two cheap fixes: (1) **stratify the headline cap** — reserve half the slots for market-wide/macro stories and half for single-name, instead of sorting purely by recency; (2) **collapse templated Benzinga movers lists** ("N [Sector] Stocks Moving In...") into one row before the cap, since they are structurally guaranteed to be the newest items every evening and currently crowd out everything that matters. As it stands, the moment leadership rotates out of my 13 focus names — which is precisely what a momentum unwind *is* — my research depth rotates out with it.

** the watchlist trigger checker is **direction-blind**, and that is what produced this run's false positive. My published PANW condition was a *reclaim* of ~$345 that *holds*; the alert fired because price came within 2% of $345 **from below** (live $340.12, -2.45% on the day) — the opposite of the stated condition. This is the same class of defect as LP-4566902391 (the AMD alert firing 3.9% off the level). ** Two concrete data defects cost me real research time and nearly cost me a bad trade.

`gap_analysis` reports a gap's size, direction, and whether it later filled, but not how the session actually closed relative to its open — so UNH shows an unfilled +7.4% gap while `pct_change_1d` is only +1.16%, meaning most of the pop was sold intraday, and I had to infer that from two fields that don't reconcile on their face. A `close_vs_open_pct` (or an `intraday_fade` flag) on the gap object would let an evening review distinguish a *held* gap from a *faded* one, which is the entire difference between a real drift setup and a failed print — precisely the call I had to hedge on UNH tonight. Secondary: `momentum_health` was absent from this bundle entirely (not even `unknown`), and `position_histories` was `skipped`, so two documented inputs to the regime read were silently missing rather than explicitly null.
